title: Printed 10 by 10 grids
subject: Mathematics
unit: Spring 2: Decimals and percentages; perimeter and area; statistics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y5 lessons 37, 41, 42, 44 (Printed 10 by 10 grids)
intro: To understand how fractions with tenths and hundredths link to decimals

blocks.text: Each grid is one whole: one square is one hundredth (0.01); one column is one tenth (0.1).

questions.q: 0.45 as a fraction in simplest form?
What percentage is 12 squares out of 100?
questions.model: Teacher: per cent means out of 100, so 12 out of 100 is 12%.

questions.q: 60% as a fraction in simplest form?
Extend: write 0.4, 0.75 and 0.05 as fractions in simplest form.
Core: shade 25%, 60% and 8% of 100 grids. What is not shaded each time?
questions.model: Teacher shades 2 columns and 5 squares: 25%; not shaded 75%.

questions.q: Extend: a bar in 10 equal parts has 4 shaded. What percentage? What if it had 20 parts and 4 shaded?
Stretch: 3 colours fill a grid: red 35%, blue 48%. What percentage is green?
Core: write 30%, 45% and 90% as fractions in simplest form.
Stretch: 12% of a class is how many pupils out of 25?
Core: complete families for 3/4, 1/5 and 7/10 (decimal and %).
Extend: Ali scored 21/25, Sara 82%, Bilal 0.8. Order the scores.
Stretch: 40% of a garden is grass, 1/4 is a path, the rest is flowers. What percentage is flowers?
Big question: how can 3/4 be written as a decimal?
Big question: what does per cent mean?
questions.a: Out of 100: 37% means 37 out of every 100

questions.q: Big question: why is 25% the same as 1/4?
